_note: Firmware catalog for newsheen.site. All hosted builds are served same-origin from firmware/ (browsers CORS-block raw github fetches). Bins mirrored from scriptkitty.sh; every entry pins a sha256 the flasher verifies before writing. gate:true entries are transmit/attack-capable and require an authorization affirmation before flashing.

firmware.name: WLEDkitty
firmware.desc: The flagship cat-lamp build. Drives the 8 LEDs inside the translucent Sheen, makes them dance to sound through the onboard I²S mic, and takes a 21-key IR remote. Boots into the Pride rainbow animation with the full WLED web UI over its own Wi-Fi AP.
firmware.buildsLine: 1 image — flashed here, then set up over Wi-Fi (http://4.3.2.1)
firmware.note: The 8 LEDs run stock; sound-reactive mode needs an I²S mic on the sensor header, and the 21-key remote needs the IR receiver fitted. After flashing, join its Wi-Fi network (starts with 'WLED-', unique to your cat; password wled1234) and open http://4.3.2.1 to name your Sheen's hotspot or join your own network.

builds.label: WLEDkitty — wipes old Wi-Fi/LED config on flash

firmware.name: Newsheen Radio
firmware.desc: Internet radio for the Sheen. Streams MP3 and AAC over HTTP/HTTPS and drives the 8-LED ring from a live frequency analysis of whatever is playing, with a spinnable globe you tap to tune, 15 light effects (4 audio-reactive), and a speech synth that reads out setup. Two builds: a small one that searches an online directory, or a ~16 MB one that carries a 37,963-station atlas on the puck so the globe and country browser work with no directory service.
firmware.buildsLine: two builds — stream from an online directory, or carry the offline atlas
firmware.note: Before flashing, wire a MAX98357A amplifier to J3 (35_SDA→LRC, 36_SCL→BCLK, 37_WS→DIN, 39_SD→GAIN, 38_SCK→SD, plus GND and 3V3). Join Wi-Fi 'Newsheen-Audio' (password meowmeow); the setup page opens itself. The atlas build is ~16 MB, replaces the whole filesystem (clearing any uploaded MP3s), and takes about a minute to flash.

builds.label: directory search — streams from an online directory (~1.6 MB, v1.0.1)
offline atlas — 37,963 stations on the puck (~16 MB, ~1 min, v1.1.0)

firmware.name: Meshtastic
firmware.desc: Meshtastic for the Sheen — the ESP32-S3 puck with a Seeed Wio-SX1262 LoRa radio. An incoming mesh text message animates the 8 top LEDs; the lamp glows a node-color at boot. An optional piezo on the buzzer pad beeps on message.
firmware.buildsLine: set your region in a Meshtastic client — the radio stays off until you do
firmware.note: Needs the optional Wio-SX1262 LoRa radio fitted. Before transmitting, attach a LoRa antenna. Set your region in the Meshtastic phone app (Bluetooth) or web client — the radio stays off until you set a region.

firmware.name: MeshCore Companion
firmware.desc: MeshCore companion for the Sheen — a long-range LoRa mesh messenger. Incoming messages flash the 8 NeoPixels (and beep an optional piezo). Two builds: pair with the MeshCore phone app over Bluetooth, or connect the web/desktop client over USB serial.
firmware.buildsLine: two builds — pair over Bluetooth, or connect over USB serial
firmware.note: Needs the optional Wio-SX1262 LoRa radio fitted. Before transmitting, attach a LoRa antenna and set your region and preset in the app. The Bluetooth build pairs with PIN 123456; the USB build connects at https://client.meshcore.co.uk over Web Serial.

builds.label: Bluetooth — pair with the phone app (PIN 123456)

firmware.name: Reticulum RNode
firmware.desc: Turns the Sheen into an RNode — a host-controlled 915 MHz LoRa transceiver for the Reticulum network stack (Sideband, MeshChat, NomadNet, rnsd). Headless. This build ships pre-provisioned, so it boots as a ready RNode with no rnodeconf step and no 'device not initialised / firmware corrupt' message.
firmware.buildsLine: pre-provisioned — boots as a valid RNode, no rnodeconf
firmware.note: Needs the optional Wio-SX1262 LoRa radio fitted. Before transmitting, attach a 915 MHz antenna to the ANT pad. Point Sideband, MeshChat, NomadNet, or rnsd at the puck's USB serial port and set your region there.

firmware.name: CircuitPython
firmware.desc: Code your cat in Python — no toolchain. CircuitPython mounts the Sheen as a USB drive named CIRCUITPY; drop a code.py on it and it runs the moment you save. A friendly way to drive the 8 LEDs, read the sensor header, and build your own gadgets. Board profile: ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 (N16).
firmware.buildsLine: one 16 MB image — then edit code.py on the CIRCUITPY drive
firmware.note: This is a ~16 MB full-flash image and takes about a minute to write. After flashing, the Sheen shows up as a USB drive named CIRCUITPY — edit code.py there and save to run. The serial monitor above shows print() output and the REPL.

firmware.name: Motoko
capabilities: Transmit 802.11 frames — beacons, probe responses, and deauth — when driven by a host program
Capture full-length Wi-Fi frames, whole WPA handshakes, and PMKIDs
firmware.desc: Turns the Sheen into a browser-driven 802.11 'radio pipe' you script live over Web Serial. Sniff and visualize Wi-Fi, or (where authorized) transmit beacons, probe responses, and deauth. Ships inert — no attack tooling on the device; it only transmits when a host program drives it.
firmware.buildsLine: drive it from motoko.site over Web Serial
firmware.note: Ships inert and transmit-capable. Sniff anywhere; transmit only on hardware and networks you own or are explicitly authorized to test — doing otherwise may be illegal.

builds.label: Motoko radio pipe — transmit-capable, ships inert

firmware.name: Bit Pirate
capabilities: Actively drive I²C / SPI / UART / 1-Wire / JTAG buses on attached hardware
Transmit infrared (and LoRa, if a Wio-SX1262 is added)
firmware.desc: The 'Swiss Army knife' hardware-hacking multitool (inspired by the Bus Pirate), on the Sheen. Talk to I²C / SPI / UART / 1-Wire / JTAG chips, blast infrared, and drive the 8-LED ring — all from a CLI over USB or the puck's Wi-Fi web terminal. 26 modes. Works stock, no radio needed; add a Wio-SX1262 and it does LoRa too.
firmware.buildsLine: boots to the 'HIZ>' CLI over USB serial @115200
firmware.note: Transmit-capable (infrared) and it actively drives attached buses — works stock, no radio needed. Only probe or transmit against hardware you own or are authorized to test. Its LoRa modes need a Wio-SX1262 added.

firmware.name: Bad Nugget (BadUSB)
capabilities: Inject real keystrokes into any computer it is plugged into (DuckyScript payloads)
Detect the host OS and adapt payloads; drive over Wi-Fi web UI or a BLE remote
firmware.desc: BadUSB keystroke injection (DuckyScript) on the screenless Sheen. No display — the 8-pixel ring is the status output (warm-white idle, red while a payload runs). Drive it over its Wi-Fi web UI (payload editor + upload) or drop .txt payloads on its USB drive. BLE remote + per-device PIN + host-OS detection included.
firmware.buildsLine: join Wi-Fi 'Newsheen' (password nugget123) to edit/run payloads
firmware.note: This injects real keystrokes into whatever computer it's plugged into. Only use it on computers you own or are explicitly authorized to test.
